title: Estimation
summary: [[rounding|Rounding]] swaps a number for a simpler one close to it: to the nearest $1000$, to [[decimal-place|decimal places]] or to [[significant-figure|significant figures]]. An [[estimate|estimate]] rounds every number to $1$ significant figure, so you can work it out in your head.

goals.text: Round to the nearest $10$, $100$ or $1000$, and to a given number of decimal places.
Round to a given number of significant figures.
Estimate a calculation by writing each number to $1$ significant figure.
Choose a sensible accuracy for an answer in context: whole things, money, measurements.

synonyms: estimate by rounding to 1 significant figure
rounding up or down in context

before.prompt: What is the value of the digit $8$ in $5.384$?
before.hint: Name the columns after the point: tenths, hundredths, thousandths.
before.explain: The $8$ is in the hundredths column, so it is worth $\frac{8}{100} = 0.08$.

before.hint: In [[standard-form|standard form]], $\times 10^{4}$ moves the digits $4$ places to the left.

sections.heading: Rounding to a place value or decimal places

blocks.text: A town of $42\,718$ people has about $43\,000$. That is [[rounding|rounding]]: simpler, but still close.

blocks.statement: To round to a given place, take the two values either side that stop at that place, and choose the nearer. Exactly halfway rounds up.

blocks.text: 1. Find the last digit you keep. Call it the rounding digit.
2. Look only at the next digit to its right. If it is $5$ or more, add $1$ to the rounding digit. If it is $4$ or less, leave the rounding digit alone.
3. Before the decimal point, dropped digits become $0$, so the number keeps its size. After the point, just drop them.

blocks.question: Write $83\,529$ correct to the nearest thousand.
steps: The thousands digit is $3$, so you keep $83$ thousands.
The next digit is $5$. That is $5$ or more, so round up: $83$ becomes $84$.
Fill the other places with zeros. Check: $83\,529$ is nearer $84\,000$ than $83\,000$.

blocks.text: Writing $84$ or $84\,529$. Every dropped place becomes $0$: $84\,000$.

blocks.prompt: Write $15\,649$ correct to the nearest hundred.
blocks.hint: The hundreds digit is $6$. Which digit decides, and is it $5$ or more?
blocks.explain: The tens digit $4$ decides, so the $6$ stays: $15\,600$. The $9$ doesn't matter.

blocks.text: [[decimal-place|Decimal places]] are the digits after the point: $5.384$ has $3$. To round to $2$ decimal places, keep $2$ of them.

blocks.question: Write $12.6973$ correct to $2$ decimal places.
steps: Keep two digits after the point: $12.69$. The next digit is $7$.
$7$ is $5$ or more, so add $1$ to the $9$. That makes $10$: write $0$ and carry $1$, giving $12.70$.
Keep the final $0$: it shows $2$ decimal places.

blocks.hint: Keep $0.39$, then look at the next digit.
blocks.explain: The next digit is $5$, so the $9$ goes up and carries: $0.40$. $0.4$ shows only $1$ decimal place.

blocks.text: $0.000\,0384$ to $2$ decimal places is $0.00$, which tells you nothing. Significant figures count from where the number really starts.

blocks.statement: The first [[significant-figure|significant figure]] of a number is its first non-zero digit, reading from the left. Every digit after it is significant too, zeros included, except zeros at the end of a whole number that only fill places: $28\,000$ to $2$ significant figures has just $2$.
blocks.plain: Start counting at the first digit that isn't $0$.

blocks.text: So $0.0507$ has $3$ significant figures: $5$, $0$ and $7$. Round as before, keeping the zeros in front and filling with zeros up to the point.

blocks.question: Write $0.006\,381$ correct to $2$ significant figures.
steps: The first significant figure is $6$, and the second is $3$.
Look at the next digit, $8$. It is at least $5$, so the $3$ becomes $4$.
Keep the zeros in front of the $6$.

blocks.hint: The second significant figure is the $7$.
blocks.explain: The next digit is $8$, so $27$ thousand becomes $28$ thousand: $28\,000$.

blocks.text: On Papers $3$ and $4$, give answers that aren't exact to $3$ significant figures, unless told otherwise. Angles go to $1$ decimal place and money to the cent. Write down the full display, then round once, at the end.

blocks.question: Use your calculator to work out $\dfrac{9.14 + 2.7^{2}}{5.3 - 1.86}$. Give your answer correct to $3$ significant figures.
steps: Put brackets round the top and the bottom: $(9.14 + 2.7^{2}) \div (5.3 - 1.86)$.
Write down the full display: $4.776162791$.
The first three significant figures are $4$, $7$ and $7$. The next digit is $6$, so the second $7$ goes up to $8$.

blocks.hint: Keep $3.99$. The next digit is $6$, so add $1$ to the last $9$.
blocks.explain: $3.99 + 0.01 = 4.00$. You need all three figures, so $4$ and $4.0$ are not enough.

blocks.text: An [[estimate|estimate]] is a rough answer you can work out in your head. It also shows whether a calculator answer is sensible.
Round every number to $1$ significant figure. Write the rounded calculation down. Then work it out.

blocks.question: Estimate $6.83 \times 31.4$ by rounding each number to $1$ significant figure.
steps: To $1$ significant figure, $6.83 \to 7$ and $31.4 \to 30$.
Write the new calculation: $7 \times 30$.
$7 \times 30 = 210$. A calculator gives $214.462$, so the estimate is close.

blocks.text: Rounding to $2$ significant figures, such as $6.83 \to 6.8$. Use one non-zero digit per number.

blocks.question: Round each number to $1$ significant figure to estimate $\dfrac{58.6 + 21.7}{0.192 \times 4.38}$. Show all your working.
steps: Write the estimate with the rounded values: $\dfrac{60 + 20}{0.2 \times 4}$.
Multiply top and bottom by $10$: $\dfrac{80}{0.8} = \dfrac{800}{8} = 100$.

blocks.prompt: A rectangular field measures $48.2$ m by $19.6$ m. Round each length to $1$ significant figure to estimate its area in $\text{m}^{2}$.
blocks.hint: Round each length to one non-zero digit, then multiply.
blocks.explain: $48.2 \to 50$ and $19.6 \to 20$, so the area is about $50 \times 20 = 1000\text{ m}^{2}$.

blocks.prompt: Estimate $\sqrt{8.9 \times 4.1}$, rounding each number to $1$ significant figure.
blocks.hint: Round both numbers first, multiply, then take the square root.
blocks.explain: $9 \times 4 = 36$ and $\sqrt{36} = 6$. $6.04$ uses the exact numbers, so it isn't an estimate.

blocks.text: A calculator gives many digits. The context tells you how many to keep.
Whole things, like coaches, need a whole number. If rounding down would leave something out, round up.
Money goes to the nearest cent, $2$ decimal places. Otherwise use the accuracy asked for, or $3$ significant figures.

blocks.question: $187$ students and $9$ teachers go on a trip. Each coach holds $45$ people. How many coaches are needed?
steps: Total people: $187 + 9 = 196$.
$4$ coaches hold only $180$ people, so $16$ would be left behind. Round up to $5$ coaches.

blocks.question: Fuel costs $\$1.389$ per litre. Ana buys $42$ litres. Work out how much she pays.
steps: Money needs $2$ decimal places. The next digit is $8$, so round up.

blocks.prompt: A pack of $6$ pens costs $\$4.15$. Work out the cost of one pen, to the nearest cent.
blocks.explain: $4.15 \div 6 = 0.6916\ldots$ The third decimal is $1$, so one pen costs $\$0.69$.

blocks.prompt: A ribbon $5$ m long is cut into pieces $0.35$ m long. How many complete pieces can be cut?
blocks.hint: Work out $5 \div 0.35$. Can a part-piece count?
blocks.explain: $5 \div 0.35 = 14.28\ldots$ Only complete pieces count, so round down: $15$ pieces would need $5.25$ m.

blocks.text: Look at the digit after the last one you keep: $5$ or more, round up; $4$ or less, leave it.
Decimal places count digits after the point. Significant figures count from the first non-zero digit.
Keep the size: $83\,529 \approx 84\,000$ to the nearest thousand. Keep the zeros asked for: $12.6973 \approx 12.70$ to $2$ d.p.
Estimate: write each number to $1$ significant figure, write the rounded calculation down, then work it out.
In context: whole things get a whole number, rounded up or down as needed. Money to the cent; otherwise the accuracy asked for, or $3$ significant figures.

mistakes: Chopping instead of rounding: $2.7486$ to $3$ significant figures is $2.75$, not $2.74$.
Counting the zeros at the front: the first significant figure of $0.0362$ is the $3$, so to $1$ significant figure it is $0.04$.
Rounding a $5$ down. When the next digit is $5$, round up: $3.5 \to 4$ to $1$ significant figure.
Rounding to the wrong place: $38\,612$ to the nearest hundred is $38\,600$, not $39\,000$ or $38\,610$. Find the hundreds digit first.
In an estimate, rounding only some of the numbers. Every number goes to $1$ significant figure.
examTips: Estimating "to $1$ significant figure": write the rounded calculation down before the answer. That line earns a method mark.
"Give your answer correct to $3$ significant figures": write down the full display first, then round. Never round in the middle of a calculation.
"Write ... correct to the nearest hundred" needs only the rounded number, with its zeros.
In a context question, check your answer makes sense: whole coaches, money to the cent.
